about: measure contests of 2024 in Ohio, in the layout of plan/PLAN.md section 3 with the fields data/README.md adds (D3). Built by pipeline/local_medsl.py from pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py's cache.

medsl.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab, Precinct-Level Returns 2024 by Individual State, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/NYTPDU, version 1.0
medsl.note: precinct returns compiled by MEDSL from each state's official sources (named per state in its README); added up to the contest by pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py, files 2024-oh-precinct-general.csv

model.name: the model's own forecast, method D3-v1.1
model.note: each year forecast from a fit on earlier years only; no polls are used

klarner.name: Carl Klarner, State Legislative Election Returns, 1967-2022, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/FJOGJB, v1.0, released 2024-06-12T21:56:14Z (the races route (a) is fitted on)

source.name: Supreme Court of Ohio: State ex rel. Citizens Not Politicians v. Ohio Ballot Bd., 2024-Ohio-4547 (decided September 16, 2024), which sets out the Ohio Ballot Board's ballot language for Issue 1. Used because ohiosos.gov (the Ballot Board's publisher) refused us (403 'access ... has been blocked').

ballot_text.source_title: Issue 1 (the Ballot Board's heading, shown as an image on the opinion's pp. 4-6: 'To create an appointed redistricting commission not elected by or subject to removal by the voters of the state - Proposed Constitutional Amendment - Proposed by Initiative Petition'; the Court says the Secretary of State sets the 'ballot title' separately)
ballot_text.type_quote: On November 5, 2024, Ohio voters will consider Issue 1, a constitutional amendment proposed by initiative petition.

fact.quote: By a three-to-two vote, the ballot board approved language for the proposed constitutional amendment.
fact.why: Inferred, not stated: the opinion describes one set of ballot language for one amendment and never mentions art. II sec. 1e or a second question. The ballot language itself is printed in the PDF as images (pp. 4-6; no text layer, so not text-checkable) and, as I read the images, carries one YES/NO box reading 'SHALL THE AMENDMENT BE APPROVED?' and the line 'A majority yes vote is necessary for the amendment to pass.' Sec. 1e(B)(2) would have made the Board 'prescribe two separate questions' (saved codes.ohio.gov text: oh_const_2_1e.html). The Ballot Board's own records at ohiosos.gov were refused, so this rests on the Court's account.

threshold.rule: majority of the electors voting thereon
threshold.quote: Any proposed law or amendment to the constitution submitted to the electors as provided in 1a and 1b, if approved by a majority of the electors voting thereon, shall take effect thirty days after the election at which it was approved and shall be published by the secretary of state.
threshold.matched: by the type the ballot text states (amendment; data/measure/ballot-texts.json); the ballot text shows it is not an initiated amendment the ballot board finds to conflict with art. II sec. 1e(B)(1) (put as two questions) [inferred] (data/measure/ballot-texts.json); proposed by the initiative [stated: the ballot text read, data/measure/ballot-texts.json], so Ohio Const. art. II, sec. 1b governs (initiated statute and initiated constitutional amendment)

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures
p.note: this route's back-test of statewide measures shows more near-even finishes than it forecast (12 against 9.1 within 1 point of ½, and 11 against 6.9 within 20,000 votes, 2018 to 2024), so p may be low
